name: bottom_quark

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Standard Model gauge group SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y with electroweak symmetry breaking, CKM unitarity, and color confinement defining the complete kinematic and dynamic arena for bottom quark production, propagation, decay, and detection

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state before the Higgs mechanism generates bottom quark mass and Yukawa coupling; no flavor quantum numbers, no CKM matrix, no weak decay channels exist

⊣.chosen_element: Standard Model Lagrangian with EWSB and confinement
⊣.justification: The closed boundary containing all gauge interactions, Yukawa couplings, CKM mixing, and non-perturbative confinement that govern the complete bottom quark lifecycle from production to detection

≻.justification: Forward morphism representing Dirac evolution from production vertex (gg → b b̄, q q̄ → b b̄) through spacetime to weak decay vertex, directed by the SM equations of motion

≺.justification: Contravariant reversal mapping b → c/u W⁻ decay amplitude to anti-b → anti-c/anti-u W⁺, the descent transformation in flavor-changing weak current space for CP asymmetry measurement

⋈.justification: Composition of production vertex → fermion propagator → weak decay vertex → W propagator → final state vertex, chained by perturbative expansion in α_s and α_weak

⊙.justification: The bottom quark recognizes itself as a mass eigenstate with definite bottomness B = -1, charge -1/3, mass 4.18 GeV, and CKM row (V_ub, V_cb, V_tb); the stone that knows its own quantum numbers

∈.chosen_element: CKM-split weak decay channels b → c W⁻ and b → u W⁻
∈.justification: The single bottom quark flavor eigenstate opens into two distinct weak decay arms weighted by |V_cb|² ≈ 0.0016 and |V_ub|² ≈ 1.6×10⁻⁵, the co-multiplication δ of flavor into mass eigenstate channels

∋.justification: The decay products (c/u quarks + W⁻) recombine with spectator quarks into color-singlet B hadrons (B⁰, B⁺, B_s⁰, Λ_b⁰, Ξ_b, Ω_b), the multiplication μ that fuses partonic arms into observable final states

⊤.justification: The affirmative arm: constructive truth of the dominant decay channel depositing T in the register as the primary weak transition with branching fraction ~99%

⊥.justification: The negative arm: constructive falsity of the dominant channel depositing F as the suppressed alternative that nevertheless occurs with measurable rate

⊞.chosen_element: quantum interference in B⁰-B⁰bar mixing and decay
⊞.justification: The paradice B-state: both b → c and b → u amplitudes coexist in the same quantum superposition, generating CP-violating asymmetries (sin2β, γ, α) and direct CP violation in B → Kπ, ππ, ρπ decays

⊡.chosen_element: silicon vertex detector measurement of displaced B decay vertex
⊡.justification: Irreversible ROM fixation: the pixel/strip tracker records the displaced secondary vertex (cτ ≈ 450 μm), permanently fixing flavor tag, lifetime, decay topology, and momentum in the experimental record

phase_2.split_element: CKM-split weak decay channels b → c W⁻ and b → u W⁻
phase_2.split_input: bottom quark flavor eigenstate with definite mass, charge, bottomness, and CKM couplings
phase_2.fuse_element: hadronization into B mesons and baryons via color confinement
phase_2.fuse_result: color-singlet hadronic final states (B⁰, B⁺, B_s⁰, Λ_b⁰, Ξ_b⁰, Ξ_b⁻, Ω_b⁻) with definite flavor quantum numbers and measurable lifetimes
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Pre-EWSB vacuum: no bottom quark mass, no Yukawa coupling, no flavor quantum numbers, no CKM matrix, no weak decay channels — the empty state before the Higgs mechanism
phase_3.true_description: Affirmative: flavor-conserving strong/EM vertex allowed (b + g → b + g, b + γ → b + γ); CKM-favored weak decay b → c W⁻ occurs with expected rate and branching fraction; B hadron reconstructed with correct mass and vertex
phase_3.false_description: Negative: flavor-changing neutral current forbidden at tree level (b → s γ loop-suppressed); CKM-suppressed decay b → u W⁻ occurs but with rate ~100× smaller; flavor tag contradicts production flavor (wrong-sign decay)
phase_3.both_description: Paradice: quantum superposition of b → c and b → u amplitudes in B⁰-B⁰bar mixing box diagram and interference decays (B → Kπ, ππ, ρπ), generating CP violation (sin2β, γ, α) — both T and F held simultaneously in the interference term, measured as time-dependent asymmetry

steps.domain_action: Initialize pre-EWSB vacuum — clear all flavor quantum numbers, zero Yukawa sector, register = 00 (N)
Bottom quark mass eigenstate self-identifies — deposits quantum numbers (B=-1, Q=-1/3, m=4.18 GeV, CKM row) into register as T (01)
Bottom quark propagates forward — Dirac evolution from production vertex (gg → b b̄ at LHC) toward decay vertex through SM background
CKM matrix splits weak decay vertex — opens T-arm for b → c W⁻ (|V_cb|) and F-arm for b → u W⁻ (|V_ub|)
T-arm evaluates — deposits constructive truth of favored decay channel, register receives T
Compose W⁻ propagator with leptonic decay — W⁻ → ℓ⁻ ν̄_ℓ chains weak vertex to semileptonic final state
F-arm evaluates — deposits constructive falsity of favored channel (suppressed channel occurs), register receives F
Quantum interference engages — both amplitudes coexist in B⁰-B⁰bar mixing box diagram, register holds B (11) as paradice
CP-conjugate reversal — maps process to anti-b → anti-c/anti-u W⁺, clears register but retains open FSPLIT frame for CP asymmetry
⋈: High-fidelity gauge vertex — commutator [Q_em, Q_weak] = 0 enforces deterministic coupling at each vertex, fidelity 𐑐
⊤: High kinetic barrier — flavor identity frozen on strong/EM timescales (τ ≫ Λ_QCD⁻¹), gate_open only for weak interaction
∈: Local interaction granularity — correlation length ~1 fm (hadron scale) or ~10⁻³ fm (W Compton wavelength), no long-range propagation
∋: Disjunctive partner selection — couples to any gauge boson (g, W, Z, γ) or quark partner allowed by conservation laws
Hadronization fuses partonic arms — color confinement recombines c/u quarks with spectators into B hadrons (B⁰, B⁺, B_s, Λ_b)
Vertex detector fixes decay vertex — silicon tracker records displaced vertex (cτ ~ 450 μm), permanent ROM record of flavor tag and lifetime
Final state self-identifies — reconstructed B meson knows its own mass, momentum, decay topology, and flavor tag
Standard Model boundary closes — all gauge interactions, CKM unitarity, confinement, and detection satisfied; system contained

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The Standard Model Lagrangian with electroweak symmetry breaking — translates gauge symmetries, Yukawa couplings, and CKM matrix into Feynman rules for bottom quark vertices and hadronization models
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Gauge boson exchange (gluons for strong, W/Z for weak, photon for EM) — components communicate via local vertex interactions mediated by gauge fields; detector readout via electronic signal propagation
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Quantum field state space (Fock space) — stores flavor quantum numbers, momentum, spin, and color on asymptotic states; silicon detector stores classical measurement records; trigger system stores event metadata
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Perturbative expansion in α_s and α_weak — orders operations by loop level (tree → 1-loop → 2-loop) and time-ordering in Dyson series; experimental trigger schedules event recording by p_T and vertex displacement thresholds
phase_5.alfs_store: Particle Data Group (PDG) Review of Particle Physics — canonical reference for bottom quark mass, CKM elements, branching fractions, lifetimes, hadron spectroscopy, and CP violation parameters

phase_6.cycle_cost: One weak interaction vertex (W exchange) per decay cycle; ~1.5 ps lifetime per bottom hadron; ~10⁴ ionization electrons per vertex detector hit
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Coherent bottom quark flavor eigenstate produced in high-energy collision (LHC pp → b b̄ + X at √s = 13 TeV) with definite momentum, quantum numbers, and production vertex
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Decohered hadronic final state (B hadrons + decay products) with measured secondary vertex, flavor tag, momentum, and CP asymmetry observables; quantum superposition collapsed by measurement
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The weak decay is unitary at the fundamental level (S-matrix unitary); entropy increase appears only in the coarse-grained hadronic final state, detector measurement, and coarse-graining over unobserved degrees of freedom, not in the microscopic quantum evolution

⊣=𐑡: The bottom quark participates in the Standard Model's gauge interaction network, connecting via strong, weak, and electromagnetic forces to other quarks, leptons, and gauge bosons in a mixed connectivity pattern without hierarchical containment or cyclic closure.
⊢=𐑼: The bottom quark is treated as a point-like particle in the Standard Model, with no internal spatial extent, operating as a local excitation of quantum fields at a single spacetime point.
⊞=𐑳: The bottom quark participates in fundamentally asymmetric interactions, such as weak decays where a single bottom quark transforms into a charm or up quark while emitting a W boson, and strong interactions where it pairs with a single antiquark in mesons or two other quarks in baryons, never exhibiting equal symmetric pairing or higher-order symmetric oligomeric stoichiometry.
⊡=𐑴: The bottom quark's role is defined by discrete, conserved quantum numbers (baryon number, electric charge, flavor) that cannot be continuously deformed to a trivial state; changing its identity requires crossing a topological boundary in the space of quantum states, analogous to Z2-protected invariants where only discrete transitions are allowed.
⊙=𐑢: The bottom quark exists as a stable, massive particle in the Standard Model's normal operating regime, exhibiting no scale-free correlations, divergent susceptibilities, or critical fluctuations; its properties are well-described by perturbative and lattice QCD far from any phase transition or critical threshold.
⊥=𐑖: The bottom quark exhibits persistent chirality through its participation in the electroweak interaction, where left-handed and right-handed components couple differently to the W and Z bosons, a structurally enforced asymmetry protected by the gauge symmetry of the Standard Model that cannot be thermally interconverted at low energies.
≻=𐑑: The bottom quark undergoes fundamental structural transformations via weak interactions, such as flavor-changing decays (b → c/u + W⁻) where its identity is irreversibly altered, and participates in strong interaction bond formation into hadrons (mesons/baryons) through color confinement, both representing irreversible or semi-reversible structural transformations rather than soft associations or catalytic stabilization.
≺=𐑿: The bottom quark carries a signed directional character through its negative electric charge (−1/3) and distinct flavor quantum number, acting as a fermionic source for gauge fields (donating color, weak isospin, and electromagnetic charge) without simultaneously accepting the same quantum numbers in a self-complementary manner.
⋈=𐑐: The bottom quark's interactions are governed by precise gauge symmetries and conservation laws (color, flavor, charge) that enforce deterministic vertex rules in the Standard Model Lagrangian, resulting in near-certain, geometry-enforcing coupling strengths and decay channels with minimal probabilistic ambiguity at the fundamental level.
⊤=𐑧: The bottom quark's flavor identity is protected by a high kinetic barrier; it cannot spontaneously rearrange into lighter quarks without the mediation of the weak interaction (W boson exchange), making flavor-changing processes rare and kinetically suppressed at low energies, effectively freezing its identity on strong and electromagnetic timescales.
∈=𐑲: The bottom quark's fundamental interactions (strong, weak, electromagnetic) occur at local vertices in quantum field theory, with correlation lengths limited to the femtometer scale of hadrons or the Compton wavelength of the W/Z bosons, influencing no neighbors beyond the immediate interaction event.
∋=𐑜: The bottom quark engages in disjunctive partner selection, coupling to any gauge boson (gluon, W, Z, photon) or any quark/antiquark partner allowed by conservation laws, with no requirement for simultaneous multi-partner assembly or strict sequential ordering.
